standard_prerequisites.name: The preimage of an ideal under a map of modules is computed by the kernel of the induced map to the quotient
standard_prerequisites.use: Rewrites the preimage in the two forms whose comparison produces the result.

core_obligations: Write the intersection of the image of the base changed map with I^n N tensor B as the image of the corresponding preimage (proof lines 292-296).

Identify that preimage with the kernel of the base changed map into the base change of the quotient N/I^n N, and use flatness of B over A to rewrite it as the tensor product of f^{-1}(I^n N) with B (proof lines 296-303).

Apply the hypothesis that c works for f over A to conclude that the intersection is contained in the image of the kernel plus I^{n-c} times the target after base change, which is the assertion (proof lines 303-308).

The nearest public record is 304 (194-245, tag 07VE, stability of exact complexes under Artin-Rees controlled perturbation), which is the preceding statement of the same section and ends 38 lines before this card's statement begins.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a base change statement for the Artin-Rees lemma: if c works for a map f of finite modules over a Noetherian ring A, then c works for the base changed map over a flat Noetherian A-algebra B with respect to the extended ideal IB (statement lines 283-290). The proof is an 18-line computation with preimages and kernels (proof lines 292-309): it writes the intersection of the image of the base changed map with I^n N tensor B as the image of the preimage under the base changed map, identifies that preimage with the tensor product of the preimage f^{-1}(I^n N) with B by using that B is flat over A, and then applies the hypothesis on c over A. The whole content is the middle step, since flatness is exactly what allows kernels to be computed before tensoring, and the author states that commutation in one sentence.
